simple.meaning: שָׁפָה (shâphâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to abrade , i.e. bare.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Job, Isaiah, beginning at Job 33:21. The surrounding contexts include mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁפָה (H8192) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁפָה (shâphâh) / H8192 is traced through Job 33:21, Isaiah 13:2 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8192. shaphah I. [ שָׁפָה ] verb sweep bare (Arabic (), of wind, raise and carry off dust, of horse, scanty in hair of forelock; Late Hebrew Pi`el plane off ; Aramaic Passive participle level ( Isa 40:4 = מִישׁוֺר ), smooth, limpid , make level, smooth (and derivatives)); — Niph`al be wind-swept, bare; Participle הַרנִֿשְׁמֶּה Isa 13:2 a bare mountain ; Pu`al Perfect consecutive עַצְמֹתָיו וְשֻׁפוּ Job 33:21 Qr his bones are laid bare (so lean is he; Kt וּשְׁפִי bareness are his bones).
